claims.text: Press TV: 'US attack on Iranian commercial vessel kills one, injures four'
claims.note: Press TV, 13 September 08:39 UTC: one killed, four injured off Qeshm Island; Iranian officials blamed the 'American-Zionist enemy'. US involvement is Iran's attribution only. IRIB via AZERTAC said one killed, three injured (https://azertag.az/en/xeber/4410864).

claims.text: Victim named Mohammad Reza Hafezi, 34-year-old deckhand
claims.note: Press TV gives no name or age. Invented.

claims.text: Vessel named Al-Sahra
claims.note: Press TV does not name the vessel. Invented.

claims.text: Strike happened on 12 September
claims.note: Press TV says around 5am local time (0130 GMT) on 13 September.

claims.text: Struck by a 'US missile' off the Strait of Hormuz
claims.note: Press TV says a self-propelled underwater missile/projectile hit the ship off Qeshm Island near the strait; attribution to US is by Iranian officials, not established.

claims.text: Three of the injured had shrapnel lodged in their throats
claims.note: Not in Press TV. Invented.

claims.text: Death certificate lists 'exsanguination secondary to missile fragment trauma'
claims.note: Invented.

claims.text: Luis Ramirez, American veteran in Jordan, leg ripped off by IRGC missile; took first unassisted steps; Press TV crew filmed; quote 'I can walk again...'
claims.note: Invented person and quote (recurring). US officials said no American personnel were killed in the 8 September Jordan attack (https://www.airandspaceforces.com/iran-damages-a-10-f-15s-with-missile-attack-on-air-base-in-jordan/).

claims.text: Aid-for-arms pipeline funds the rockets that maimed him
claims.note: Invented link.

claims.text: Iraqi MP Saad Al-Mousawi announced US forces will leave by 30 September
claims.note: No MP of that name found making this statement. The 30 September date itself was set by Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi and US officials in August (https://www.local10.com/news/world/2026/08/12/officials-say-us-forces-on-track-to-complete-iraq-pullout-by-sept-30/).

claims.text: US forces to leave Iraq by 30 September
claims.note: AP, 12 August 2026.

claims.text: Timetable 'aligns suspiciously' with the Al-Sahra incident; US 'withdrew from Iraq a decade ago'
claims.note: Invented link; US forces were present until 30 September 2026.

claims.text: Iran's 'president-elect' Mohammad Pezeshkian
claims.note: Masoud Pezeshkian is Iran's president, in office since 2024, not president-elect; first name is Masoud.

claims.text: BRICS summit in Johannesburg
claims.note: Summit was in New Delhi, 12-13 September 2026.

claims.text: Pezeshkian demanded 'genuine reform of international mechanisms' and defence of the non-use of force principle; urged BRICS to play a more active role
claims.note: Tasnim quoted 'We need real reform of international mechanisms'. Press TV: multilateralism loses meaning when the UN Charter fails to shield countries from unlawful military action. Wording in edition paraphrased.

claims.text: Xi Jinping called for peace in West Asia at the summit
claims.note: Xi urged BRICS to take a peacemaking role in the Middle East war, 12 September.

claims.text: Middle East Eye reported Israeli settlers stormed Al-Aqsa under police protection on 13 September
claims.note: No MEE report for that date found; similar incursions are reported frequently by Jordanian outlets but none dated 13 September.

claims.text: Palestinian carpenter Youssef Al-Hassan, 28, beaten near Ramallah, left eye knocked out
claims.note: No source found. Invented.

claims.text: AI sentiment 63, conflict mood 45, Bitcoin sentiment 54, market signal 48
claims.note: Internal scores; no public source.

claims.text: Brent's climb past $106, noted by The Defiant
claims.note: No Defiant article giving $106 found; no dated price source.

claims.text: SEC crypto custody rewrite under White House review
Revolut's EURR launch
DW video 'LIVE: Donald Trump's AI Data Center Push Sparks Fierce Backlash Across America'
claims.note: Feed video title; not verified. Edition also calls Trump a 'former president', which is wrong (he is the sitting president).

claims.text: Ex-Anthropic researcher told the BBC AI staff are 'genuinely frightened' for humanity's future
claims.note: Jacob Coxon, interviewed by Laura Kuenssberg (BBC), 13 September; republished BBC text. 'Genuinely frightened' is the BBC's paraphrase in its lead, not a direct Coxon quote; he said staff feel trapped in a race. BBC page itself not fetched.

claims.text: Fisherman's family sells fish from a freezer in Bandar Abbas
claims.note: Invented.

claims.text: BRICS summit will vote tomorrow on a new development bank charter funding Iran's missile factories
claims.note: No source; summit ended 13 September with the New Delhi Declaration.

claims.text: Celebratory fireworks in Baghdad on 30 September
claims.note: Speculation, unsupported.

claims.note: No source found.

edits.headline: Iran says attack on cargo ship off Qeshm Island kills 1
edits.subheadline: Four other people were injured when the ship was hit at about 5am local time near the Strait of Hormuz, Press TV reported.
editorialBody: One person was killed and four were injured when an Iranian commercial vessel was hit off Qeshm Island in the Persian Gulf on 13 September, Press TV reported.
Iranian officials blamed US and Israeli forces. Qeshm Island governor Hossein Amir-Teymouri said further details would be released after investigations, Press TV reported.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told a closed BRICS leaders' session in New Delhi on 12 September that multilateralism loses meaning when the UN Charter fails to shield countries from unlawful military action, Press TV reported.
Chinese President Xi Jinping urged BRICS to take a peacemaking role in the Middle East war, Al-Monitor reported on 12 September.
Jacob Coxon, a researcher who resigned from Anthropic, told the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg that people at AI companies feel trapped in a race and fear where it leads.
US and Iraqi officials said in August that US forces were on track to complete their withdrawal from Iraq by 30 September, the Associated Press reported.
